hosting.//: The blog and its CMS, served at the ROOT of their own origin. They used to live under odoapp.in/blog; moving them to a subdomain is what makes this a site rather than a subdirectory, and the app already handles it — basePathOf() returns an empty base when the path does not start with /blog.
hosting.//redirects: Anything still asking for /blog/<slug> on THIS origin is an old link that was rewritten by hand or bookmarked mid-migration. Sent to the same slug at the root rather than 404ing. The redirects that matter for search live on the landing site, which is where the old URLs actually were.
hosting.//rewrites: Static files win, so a pre-rendered /<slug>.html is served to a crawler before this ever fires. Everything unmatched falls through to the app.
hosting.//headers: Sources must not overlap. The CSP names one Supabase project, never both: a policy listing the pair would let a build configured for the wrong environment reach it silently.

headers.value: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self' https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com https://securetoken.googleapis.com https://kxxgfhwnidgfvjowqaad.supabase.co; img-src 'self' data: https://kxxgfhwnidgfvjowqaad.supabase.co; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self' data:; worker-src 'self' blob:; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'

headers.//: Content-hashed, so the name IS the version — `6e23e54….wasm` cannot ever hold different bytes. `immutable` tells the browser not even to revalidate, which removes a round trip per file on every visit after the first. These two files are 3.5 MB of the 3.6 MB a cold load costs.

A stable filename, so it must revalidate: a cached bundle can reference hashed .wasm files that no longer exist, which is a blank page with a 404 in the console. Revalidation is cheap — it answers 304 with no body.
The entry point. Firebase's hour would make a deploy invisible for an hour to anyone who had already visited.
cleanUrls serves index.html here, and it needs the same treatment.

The string table. A stable name and only 7 KB, so it revalidates rather than being pinned — every label in the app comes out of this file, and serving a stale one after a copy change is worse than one conditional request.

hosting.//site: `odo-blog` is reserved by another Firebase project — site ids are globally unique, not per-project. The id only ever shows in the .web.app fallback URL; the address people use is the custom domain.
hosting.//cache:
Cache-Control, split by whether a filename can be trusted.
Firebase's default is max-age=3600 on everything, which is wrong in both directions: too short for a content-hashed file that can never change, and too long for an entry point that has to reflect a deploy.
